title: Revert "QCDIAG: Improvements and Coverity fix" (mostly)
description:
This reverts a lot of the changes of commit db3e7964fdd4cb694a777691267f006ad6002376.
A few minor changes where made to properly use pinfo->pool memory

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 3a0d597d - Revert "QCDIAG: Improvements and Coverity fix" (mostly)
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24208/diffs?diff_id=1736228600&start_sha=7e5cfd74f27ebad52737c505cfc8b3dfa86928c9)
Please do not revert back the whole lot like this. I have been working hard on this code to kepp it simple and clean and reverting back the previous MR is not helping.

The motivation of the previous changes was just for Coverity's sake and they are not in the style of hundreds of other dissectors that successfully use val_to_str[_ext] with values outside of the value_string (which is why the printf style is used).
wmem_strbuf_t with pinfo->pool memory scope is also the preferred method for string manipulation within a packet.
Working towards a "model" or whatever can tell Coverity these are not real problems is a better use of time then playing whack-a-mole with individual dissectors and breaking the overall "coding style" of dissection.

Michael, I agree with you in some extent but I do not think I would break "coding style". I act in good faith and I think that is a bit too strong to state like that. The changes were not only for Coverity's sake, please. Some are logical improvement to me. For example:

- From `val_to_str_ext` to `val_to_str_ext_const`, several instances:
    ```
    text = val_to_str_ext_const(cmd, &qcdiag_cmds_ext, "Unknown Command");
    text = val_to_str_ext(pinfo->pool, cmd, &qcdiag_cmds_ext, "Unknown Command (0x%02x)");
    ```
    It was a mistake originally to add the hex value there. It is not needed, the tree item (`proto_item_append_text`) does not require it, the HFs provide it anyway. So as an improvement, I removed it and used `val_to_str_ext_const` which more sense. There are over 100 dissectors with `val_to_str_ext_const`. Yes, indeed, it also fixed a CID. but reverting this type of changes is not justified to me.

- I fixed some variable names because it was not correct before (e.g. it's number, major, minor correctly). Other valirbale name changes were for simplifications.
- Fixing variable type in `dissect_qcdiag_log_wcdma_rrc_states` from `uint32_t` to `uint8_t` since we work with 1 byte only
- Correcting a comment

On the other hand, yes, I agree with:
- from `tvb_get_uint32(tvb, 12, ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN)` to `(uint32_t)tvb_get_letohl(tvb, 12)`. It's a good improvement.
- to eliminate `snprintf`, I see it now and found in README too
- to use `wmem_strbuf_get_str` instead of `wmem_strbuf_finalize`


So I am asking you again, please do no rever the whole lot, let's address the real issue only which is to eliminate `snprintf` first.

I would really appreciate your support and understanding.

val_to_str_ext to val_to_str_ext_const.  There are two types of places where that's done:
1. The INFO column
2. The "parent" leaf of tree

Because there are potentially hundreds of "unknown values" (because the enumerations are small) and I presume users would like to see which ones at quick glance.  For known values, they probably don't need (or care) about the numeric value, so you shouldn't "manually" break up enumeration string and value in a separate printf-style statement.  How this is done is inconsistently applied across the hundreds of Wireshark dissectors, but let's not change one dissector in the name of "Coverity".  I'll defer to the original developers of the dissector to know what information they needed where (much as I hate the inconsistency too).  The Wireshark API should be "safe" to do it either way (and if Coverity doesn't understand that, it's a bug on its end)

To me the variable name changes were inconsequential as they are really just temporary for the printf-style formatted string and it was just faster to revert the whole change around.  I did just "keep" your variable names upon rereview, but don't think it was required.

Because the proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint[X] are newer APIs, there are still many dissectors that return a uint32 with proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint where the field is smaller and that should be fine. I would prefer to see these types of changes in a mass update, although I still think it's compiler/OS specific on how well the code performs on values < 32 bits (or now that all (most) OSes are 64-bit based).  Really you're just adding more work for the developer to make sure the length and function name match (where they had some more flexibility before because 8, 16, 24, or 32 bit values all work with proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint.)
